framework_note: J-BOOK cohort applied to QBTS. The 10-Q itself contains zero specific Pentagon-program disclosure, so we cannot fire pentagon_jbook on any named-program claim — there are no named programs to test. Instead the J-Book divergence catch here is structural: the cohort metadata asserts 'Government revenue via D-Wave Government Inc.', and the framework's verifiers show that subsidiary has ZERO contract and ZERO grant obligations as of 2023-01-15 (usaspending INFLATION_SUSPECT) and ZERO DoD-program-of-record presence (pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND across all D-Wave name variants). Quantum programs in the J-Book corpus at this cutoff are all IONQ / IONQ-subcontractor, not D-Wave. So D-Wave's 'government revenue' narrative, to the extent it exists, is Canadian (SIF) — not the J-Book exposure the cohort is built to catch. This is the orthogonal finding: framework correctly identifies QBTS as having NO J-Book exposure to lose.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave Quantum derives the majority of its revenue from the United States; for nine months ended Sept 30 2022 US revenue was $2.461M of $4.778M total (51.5%).
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_federal_presence resolved D-Wave Government Inc. UEI PATGKJM747F7 but found 0 contracts and 0 grants as of 2023-01-15; signal INFLATION_SUSPECT for federal-presence — but the claim itself was 'US revenue', which is a true geographic-revenue assertion (commercial US customers, not federal). The 10-Q does NOT claim federal-DoD revenue, so this passes as a geographic statement.
scores.interpretation: US is the largest geography by revenue, but it is commercial US revenue (universities, enterprise pilots) — not DoD. No J-Book divergence on the actual claim made.

scores.claim_text: Three significant customers accounted for 15%/11%/10% of three-month-ended Sept 30 2022 revenue (anonymized as Customer A/B/C). Top customer ~$254K Q3 2022.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook contractor_name lookups across 'D-Wave', 'D-Wave Quantum', 'D-Wave Government' all returned NOT_FOUND (corpus has 0 D-Wave programs). Per J-Book Heuristic 7: NOT_FOUND ≠ red flag — corpus may not cover this PE. But the magnitude ($254K) is too small to plausibly be a tracked Pentagon PE anyway; the absence of any program-of-record disclosure is consistent with absence in the J-Book corpus.
scores.interpretation: Customers are likely commercial / academic, not Pentagon Programs of Record. PASS — no claim to verify.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave's only disclosed material government funding is the Canadian Strategic Innovation Fund (SIF) — a C$40M repayable contribution from the CANADIAN (not US) government.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient_name='D-Wave') → 0 awards. usaspending.query_recipient_contracts(recipient_name='D-Wave Government') → 0 awards. The disclosed government source (Canadian SIF) is not a USAspending-visible US federal contract — consistent with the filing. There is no contradiction between the 10-Q disclosure and the public federal record.
scores.interpretation: The disclosure is honest about funding source: it's Canadian government (SIF), not US DoD. Framework correctly finds nothing to dispute.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave names QCaaS (Quantum Computing as a Service) and professional services as its principal revenue streams; no DoD program-of-record is named as a revenue contributor or pipeline.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook(program_name='quantum') returned 3 matches — all IONQ-related (AFRL Quantum Networking, AFRL Qubitekk, UMD Quantum/IONQ). D-Wave appears as primary contractor on ZERO of them. pentagon_jbook(program_name='AFRL Quantum Networking') returned IONQ as the sole contractor. So at cutoff D-Wave has no presence in the J-Book quantum corpus — consistent with the 10-Q claiming only commercial QCaaS revenue.
scores.interpretation: QBTS is honest about not being a J-Book Programs-of-Record contractor. PASS. (Asymmetric tell: the J-Book quantum line items are all IONQ-coded — D-Wave is not in the Pentagon's forward funding plan for quantum.)

scores.claim_text: D-Wave Quantum has substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern; trust-account redemptions reduced SPAC cash to ~$9M of ~$300M.
scores.M_check: ucc_proxy returned MODERATE_LIEN_EXPOSURE (7 secured-debt term hits across 8-K/10-K/10-Q in window, but 0 Item 2.03 events and 0 distress terms). Consistent with the disclosed Venture Loan (repaid at close) and SIF security agreements — no incremental lien activity beyond what's in the 10-Q. Going-concern language is explicitly disclosed by management; framework cannot dispute it.
scores.interpretation: Going-concern is openly disclosed. Lien proxy doesn't escalate it. PASS. (Note: this is the macro risk that backs the negative thesis — financing risk, not J-Book risk.)

scores.claim_text: D-Wave's quantum computing technology is protected by patents; the company has invested heavily in R&D (control claim).
scores.M_check: USPTO ODP: D-Wave Systems Inc. has 451 total applications and 183 granted patents as of 2023-01-15, spanning quantum annealing, qubit architecture, DAC compensation, scalable quantum computing. Strong IP corroboration.
scores.interpretation: Patent portfolio is real and substantial. Strong PASS on control claim — the underlying technology claim is not inflated.

scores.claim_text: Long-lived assets are substantially located in Canada (~95% of $10.6M) and the United States. Principal operating facility is in Canada — D-Wave is NOT a US defense-industrial-base contractor.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities(facility_name='D-Wave', state_abbr='CA') returned 31 fuzzy matches (Verizon Quartzite Microwave, White Wave Foods, etc.) — ZERO actual D-Wave Systems facilities in California. Consistent with the disclosed Canadian-HQ posture; EPA FRS does not register Canadian facilities, so absence is expected.
scores.interpretation: Facility geography matches disclosure (Canada). D-Wave is structurally not embedded in the US defense industrial base — supports the broader finding that there is no J-Book exposure to test.

scores.claim_text: D-Wave has no significant counterparty disclosure naming federal customers; customers are anonymized A/B/C. Control test: does any DoD prime mention 'D-Wave'?
scores.M_check: edgar_fts(search_term='D-Wave', cik=Lockheed 0000936468) → 0 hits in Lockheed's own SEC filings through cutoff. edgar_fts(search_term='D-Wave', all filers, through cutoff) → 116 total hits, but visible top-filings are D-Wave Quantum Inc.'s own filings and DPCM Capital (its SPAC). No DoD prime corroborates a D-Wave commercial relationship at the cutoff — consistent with the 10-Q (which does NOT claim a prime-contractor partnership).
scores.interpretation: Asymmetric finding: no Tier-1 DoD prime mentions D-Wave in pre-2023-01-15 filings — but the 10-Q never claims a prime relationship, so there's no contradiction. PASS on the (modest) claim made. The takeaway is that QBTS at cutoff has neither claimed nor possessed Pentagon J-Book exposure.

summary.headline_finding: QBTS has NO disclosed Pentagon J-Book exposure to lose. D-Wave Government Inc. UEI exists but has $0 federal awards as of 2023-01-15 (INFLATION_SUSPECT); D-Wave is absent from the J-Book quantum corpus (all 3 quantum line items are IONQ-coded). The QBTS short thesis is therefore NOT a J-Book divergence pattern — it is a going-concern / dilution / sub-scale-revenue thesis. The J-Book framework correctly returns 'no J-Book mismatch to flag here'.
